Schedule → a division → Edit bracket

The bracket editor, before and after

This is the screen in your 19 October screenshot. The schedule’s redesign redrew the bracket you read, but never the editor behind “Edit bracket”. I drew both sides from the code’s own values, at true size and in Warm. The editor is wider than most screens, so scroll each drawing sideways.

The letteringPool and round headings, the Winners / Losers tags and the Done button are all in the typewriter font, in capitals, spaced wide. The pool heading’s typed name hides under the capitals.
Text under the floorSeven pieces of text are 8.6 to 10 px: the health panel’s labels and its Show button, the time line on each game, the zoom hint. The product’s smallest size for words someone reads is 12 px.
Three field heights in one cardThe game you are editing has a 19 px code box, 23 px team boxes and 20 px date, time and field boxes. Every other admin form uses 34 px. On a phone the card already grows to 38 px. The desk is the odd one out.
The clock (a defect, fixed in this stage)Each game prints its time as the stored clock: “16:00:00 · Diamond 2”. Your clock rule says “4:00 p.m.” everywhere a customer reads a time. The spelling check misses it because the time comes from data, not from the code’s text.
Wider than lettering (call B2). The card you edit has its own small date, time and field form. The schedule’s Game window does the same job everywhere else, and in the bracket you read, clicking a game already opens it. I have drawn the card in place at full size, because that stays inside a lettering sweep. Whether the editor should hand time and place to the Game window is a separate call.

34 px, the admin’s one-line field

Proposed: one label column (Home, Away, Date, Start, Field), so the eye reads down one edge. Each field is the admin’s standard field: 34 px at the compact density (38 px at the comfortable one), 14 px text, and the field’s rounded corners. The coaches portal’s fields are 36 px by their own ruling, so 34 here is not drift. The date and time sit on their own rows, because at full size they no longer fit side by side in 220 px. They are the browser’s own controls, as in the Game window, so they show the time the way the computer is set (“10:00 AM” on one set to US English). Done becomes a standard button at the card’s foot.

The bracket’s automatic round names (“Grand Final”, “Winners Bracket”) are also the words the bracket engine matches on. The fix changes how they are displayed and leaves the stored words alone. Changing them “in the data”, as the list first said, would break that matching. This is a build note, not a call for you.

S01S02
Your calls · Stage 2, plus two from Stage 1

Eight calls

Six come from the drawings (B1 to B6). Two are Stage 1 leftovers (P1, P2). Each carries my recommendation, except the walk verdict in P2, which only you can give. Pick, add a note if you like, then build the paste-back at the bottom. Nothing gets built until you rule.

B1 · The game you are editing in the bracket

Its fields are 19, 23 and 20 px tall, with 11 to 12 px text. Every other admin form uses 34 px, and on a phone this card already grows to 38 px. How should the card look on a computer?

Rides on it: the bracket editor drawings (tab 1, close-up). The phone layout is unchanged; it already meets the size.

B2 · A second form for a game’s time and place

The editor’s card has its own date, time and field form. Everywhere else, the Game window does that job, and it checks for a clash and asks before telling teams about a change. Should the editor hand time and place to the Game window?

Rides on it: nothing in this sweep if you pick the first option. The second would go on the plan as a follow-up for the schedule.

B3 · Text smaller than the product’s floor

The bracket editor and the schedule’s health panels set words someone reads at 8.6 to 10 px: labels over figures, the Show / Hide button, a game’s time line, the zoom hint. The product’s smallest size for read text is 12 px. The tiniest size (10 px) is kept for badges, which you recognize rather than read. The sweep was about font, capitals, spacing and weight, not size. Fix the sizes too?

Rides on it: the bracket editor, the bracket and schedule health panels, the timeline.

B4 · One left edge in a round column

Today a round’s heading is centred over a 220 px column, but its games are 188 px wide and sit at the left. Nothing lines up with the heading.

Rides on it: the editor only. The bracket you read already lines up.

B5 · Winners and Losers in a double-elimination bracket

They become the band heading you ruled in A4: narrow heading font, small capitals, grey. Today the colour also tells the two brackets apart (green for winners, amber for losers).

Rides on it: the editor’s double-elimination layout (tab 1, close-up).

B6 · Round names once the capitals come off

Today every round name is forced into capitals, which hides how it was written. Once that stops, two kinds of name show: names an organizer typed (“Round 1”, “Gold medal game”), and names the bracket fills in itself (“Grand Final”, “Winners Bracket”, “Grand Final Game 2 (If Necessary)”). The playoff generator already words the automatic ones as “Final”, “Winners bracket” and “Second final, if it’s needed”.

Rides on it: the bracket editor, the bracket you read, and the public bracket. The stored words are not touched; the bracket engine matches on them.

P1 · The two pills on the top bar (held from Stage 1)

Everything else on the top bar is now in the normal font. The Workspaces pill and the public-site pill still use typewriter capitals. Those pills also appear on the public bars: the marketing site’s bar, the public tournament pages and the signed-in home bar. Those bars are all set in typewriter capitals, and they already belong to the queued “public face, warm” project.

Rides on it: the admin and coaches portal top bars. With the first option, the pill reads differently on a public page for a while. A public page already differs from the admin in every other way.

P2 · Stage 1 walk, Part C (Help): no verdict

You ticked both Help steps (the drawer’s small label and title; the Help & guides page’s title, section labels and contents headings) but did not mark Pass, Issue or Needs a call. Everything else passed.

Rides on it: closing the Stage 1 walk in the QA ledger.
